title: ai ee ie oa, and oo
overview:
New long vowels: ai, ee, ie, oa, oo.
These are the long vowels. The vowel says its own name.
Two letters. One sound.
Do not sound them out one by one.
functions: Say the sound for each new spelling
Read a word that has one in it
Write a word that has one in it
Know where in a word each one goes
Read the new words out loud
Choose between two spellings of one sound
learningPath: Words: the new long vowels and the new words.
Write the words from their sounds.
Practice and quiz. Check your answers.
lectureScript:
This is Unit 13. The long vowels.
So far every vowel was short.
Cat. Pin. Dog. Bus. Short sounds.
Now the vowel says its own name.
Listen. Ai. That is the letter a, long.
Wait. w. ai. t. Three sounds.
Not four. The ai is one sound.
Rain. r. ai. n. Three sounds.
Next. Ee. That is e, long.
Feet. f. ee. t. Three sounds.
Listen to the pair. Fit. Feet.
Fit is short. Feet is long.
Next. Ie. That is i, long.
Pie. p. ie. Two sounds only.
Next. Oa. That is o, long.
Boat. b. oa. t. Three sounds.
Listen to the pair. Got. Goat.
Last. Oo. This one has two sounds.
Listen. Boot. Now listen. Foot.
Boot is long. Foot is short.
Same two letters. Two sounds.
You cannot tell by looking.
Try the long one first. Then the short one.
One of them will be a word you know.
Now three tricky words.
Who. Love. Have.
These do not follow the sounds.
Who is not w, h, o. It is hoo.
Love does not rhyme with the word rove.
Have does not rhyme with the word gave.
Learn those three by sight.
That is Unit 13. The vowel says its name.

words.meaning: Two letters, one sound: ai. It sits in the middle of a word.
words.example: The word wait has ai in it.
practice: It is a in its own name.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor for a word with ai in it.

words.meaning: Two letters, one sound: ee. It can sit in the middle or at the end.
words.example: The word feet has ee in it.
practice: It is e in its own name.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor to say feet and fit. Say which is long.

words.meaning: Two letters, one sound: ie. It often comes at the end of a short word.
words.example: The word pie has ie in it.
practice: Tie and die end with ie.
It is i in its own name.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor for a word that ends in ie.

words.meaning: Two letters, one sound: oa. It sits in the middle of a word.
words.example: The word boat has oa in it.
practice: It is o in its own name.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor for a word with oa in it.

words.meaning: Two letters, one sound: oo. It has two sounds. Say the word and see.
words.example: The word boot has oo in it.
practice: Say oo, long, as in boot.
Say oo, short, as in foot.
Boot and foot are not the same.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor to say boot and foot. Listen.

grammar.title: The new long vowels: ai, ee, ie, oa, oo
grammar.explanation:
Two vowels together make ONE long sound.
The vowel says its own name.
Short a is in cat. Long a is in wait.
grammar.rule:
ai   as in wait     middle
ee   as in feet     middle or end
ie   as in pie      usually the end
oa   as in boat     middle
oo   as in boot     two sounds: boot, foot
grammar.workedExample:
You see ai in a word.
1. Do not read two letters.
2. Read one sound.
3. Say that sound out loud.
4. Now find it in wait.
5. Say the sound again there.
grammar.mistake:
Sounding out both letters gives no word at all.
wait is not w - a - i - t.
It is w - ai - t.
grammar.tip: Two letters. Look once. Say once.
grammar.practice:
Say the sound for each one.
1. ai
2. ee
3. ie
4. oa
5. oo
grammar.answers:
Check yourself out loud.
Did you say ONE sound each time?
Two sounds means you read the letters, not the spelling.

grammar.title: Reading a word that has ai, ee, ie, oa, oo in it
grammar.explanation:
Find the two letters first.
Read them as one sound.
Then read the rest of the word.
grammar.rule:
wait     w - ai - t
feet     f - ee - t
pie      p - ie
boat     b - oa - t
boot     b - oo - t
foot     f - oo - t
grammar.workedExample:
You see the word feet.
1. Look for the two letters.
2. Cover them with your finger.
3. Read what is left.
4. Now put the one sound back in.
5. Join it all. feet.
grammar.mistake:
Reading left to right, letter by letter, breaks here.
Look for the pair BEFORE you start.
grammar.practice:
Join the sounds and write the word.
1. w - ai - t
2. f - ee - t
3. p - ie
4. b - oa - t
5. b - oo - t
6. f - oo - t
grammar.answers:
1. wait
2. feet
3. pie
4. boat
5. boot
6. foot
Five or six right? You can read these.

grammar.title: Writing a word that has ai, ee, ie, oa, oo in it
grammar.explanation:
Say the word. Break it into sounds.
One of those sounds needs TWO letters.
Count sounds, then write.
grammar.rule:
wait     w - ai - t         3 sounds, 4 letters
feet     f - ee - t         3 sounds, 4 letters
grammar.workedExample:
You want to write pie.
1. Say it out loud.
2. Break it: p - ie.
3. Which sound needs two letters?
4. Write that pair together.
5. Read it back to check.
grammar.mistake:
One letter for each sound is wrong now.
The new sound takes two letters.
grammar.tip: Count sounds. Some need two letters.
grammar.practice:
Write the word you hear.
1. pie
2. boat
3. boot
4. foot
5. rain
6. week
grammar.answers:
1. pie
2. boat
3. boot
4. foot
5. rain
6. week
Five or six right? Good.

grammar.title: Long oo and short oo: boot and foot
grammar.explanation:
One spelling. Two sounds.
You cannot tell which by looking.
You try one, then the other.
grammar.rule:
Long oo    boot, room, food, moon
Short oo   foot, book, good, look

Both are common. Neither is wrong.
grammar.workedExample:
You see a word with oo in it.
1. Try the long one first.
2. Does that make a word you know?
3. If yes, that is it.
4. If no, try the short one.
5. One of the two will be a word.
grammar.mistake:
Deciding before you read wastes time.
Read it one way. Not a word? Read it the other way.
grammar.practice:
Long or short? Say each one out loud.
1. boot
2. foot
3. room
4. book
5. moon
6. good
grammar.answers:
1. long
2. short
3. long
4. short
5. long
6. short
Five or six right? Your ears are working.

grammar.title: Tricky words: who, love and have
grammar.explanation:
These three do not follow the sounds.
You cannot work them out.
There are not many like this.
grammar.rule:
who    said hoo, not w-h-o
love   does not rhyme with rove
have   does not rhyme with gave
grammar.workedExample:
You meet the word have.
1. Try the sounds first. Always.
2. h - a - ve. That is not a word.
3. So it is a tricky word.
4. Look at it. Say it. Look away. Say it.
5. Three times a day for three days.
grammar.mistake:
Guessing from the first letter is the trap.
Look at the whole word, then say it.
grammar.practice:
Read these by sight.
1. who
2. love
3. have
Look, say, look away, say.
grammar.answers:
There is no working out here.
Check: each one read without stopping?
Not yet? Three times a day for three days.

readings.title: A Week of Rain
readings.genre: A short text using known sounds
readings.setting: A wet week, waiting for a boat
readings.passage:
I had to wait a week.
Then I got on the boat.
It was wet. The rain did not stop.
I had wet feet in the boots.
A man on the boat had a pie.
He did not need it.
He said I can have it.
Who needs a wet pie? I do.

readings.title: Short Or Long?
readings.setting: The wall card, twelfth one along
readings.passage:
One vowel is short.
Two vowels are long.

cat   wait
fit   feet
got   boat

Say each pair out loud. Hear the long one.

comprehension.q: What is the first word in the text?
Find a word with ai in it.
comprehension.a: Any word from the text with ai in it.
comprehension.why: Look along each line for the two letters.

comprehension.q: Read line two out loud. Did you stop in the middle?
comprehension.a: Any honest answer. Stopping is normal at first.

comprehension.q: How many sounds are in boat?
comprehension.a: 3. Count what you hear, not the letters.
comprehension.why: The new spelling is one sound, not two.

comprehension.q: How many lines are in this text?
Read the text again, a little faster. Was it easier?
comprehension.a: Usually yes. The second reading is always easier.
comprehension.why: This is the point of reading it twice.

comprehension.q: Find a word you could not read last month.
comprehension.why: Looking back is how you see the progress.

comprehension.q: What does this notice ask you to do?
Do what the notice says. Did you manage it?
comprehension.why: The notice is a real instruction, not a text.

comprehension.q: Read the whole notice out loud, twice.

speaking.title: Speaking 1 — The new sounds
speaking.instructions:
Listen and repeat each sound.
ai
ee
ie
oa
oo
ONE sound each. Not two.
Now say each one three times.
Tap the mic. Say them all.
Check: one sound, or did two slip out?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to say one of the new sounds. Say it back.

speaking.title: Speaking 2 — Read the words
speaking.instructions:
Say each word two ways. Slow, then fast.
1. w - ai - t ... wait
2. f - ee - t ... feet
3. p - ie ... pie
4. b - oa - t ... boat
5. b - oo - t ... boot
6. f - oo - t ... foot
Tap the mic. Say all six both ways.
Check: was the new spelling one sound?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to say three sounds. Join them and say the word.

speaking.title: Speaking 3 — Say it, then write it
speaking.instructions:
For each word: say it, break it, write it.
1. pie
2. boat
3. boot
4. foot
5. rain
6. week
Tap the mic. Say each word and its sounds.
Check: did you say the sounds before you wrote?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor for a word with the new spelling. Break it out loud.

speaking.title: Speaking 4 — Read the list
speaking.instructions:
Read these out loud, straight down the list.
wait
feet
pie
boat
boot
foot
rain
week
Do it twice. The second time, try not to stop.
Tap the mic. Read the list twice.
Check: was the second time easier?
speaking.tutor: Read the list to the tutor. Ask which words were not clear.

speaking.title: Speaking 5 — Long oo and short oo
speaking.instructions:
Say each word. Then say long or short.
boot. foot. room. book. moon. good.
Say the word, then the word long or short.
Tap the mic. Do all six.
Check: did boot and foot come out different?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to say boot and foot. Say which is long.

speaking.title: Speaking 6 — The tricky words
speaking.instructions:
Read these by sight. Do not sound them out.
who
love
have
Look. Say. Look away. Say again.
Tap the mic. Read them all.
Check: did you read each one without stopping?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to use who in a question.

writing.title: Writing 1 — Words with the new spelling
writing.prompt:
Say each word. Break it into sounds.
Write two letters for the new sound.
writing.criteria:
Six words.
The new spelling written as a pair.
You read each one back after writing it.
writing.extension: Now write one more word with the same spelling.

writing.title: Writing 2 — Sounds and letters
writing.prompt:
Write each word. Then write two numbers.
How many sounds. How many letters.
writing.criteria:
Six words.
Two numbers beside each one.
The numbers are not the same. That is the point.
writing.extension: Find a word where they ARE the same.

Check: one sound every time?

1.
2.
3.
4.
5.
6.

activities.instructions:
Write long or short for each word.
1. boot
2. foot
3. room
4. book
5. moon
6. good
activities.answers:

2. short
3. long
4. short
5. long

Five or more right: your ears are working.
Below five: say each pair together — boot, foot.

activities.instructions:
Read this list out loud, twice.
wait
feet
pie
boat
boot
foot
rain
week
activities.answers:
There is no written key.
Check: did you read all eight?
Was the second reading faster than the first?
Stopping on a word is normal. Try again and move on.

activities.instructions:
Read these by sight.
1. who
2. love
3. have
Look, say, look away, say.
activities.answers:
There is no working out here.
Check: each one read without stopping?
Not yet? Three times a day for three days.
activities.solo: Read them out loud, then check.

quizzes.q: When you see ai you should ___.
quizzes.why: Read the pair as one, not as two letters.

quizzes.q: Join the sounds: w - ai - t. The word is ___.
quizzes.why: The sounds in order make the word.

quizzes.q: Join the sounds: f - ee - t. The word is ___.
quizzes.why: Find the pair first, then read the rest.

quizzes.q: To write a word with the new spelling you ___.
options: write two letters for that sound
write one letter for each sound
quizzes.a: write two letters for that sound
quizzes.why: The new sound is one sound and two letters.

quizzes.q: How many sounds are in boat?
quizzes.why: Count what you HEAR. There are more letters than sounds.

options: read the pair as one sound
quizzes.a: read the pair as one sound
quizzes.why: Letter by letter is the slow way here.

quizzes.q: You cannot read a word. What do you do first?
quizzes.why: Find the pair, then read around it.

quizzes.q: Boot and foot both have oo. The sound is ___.
quizzes.why: One is long, one is short. Same spelling.

quizzes.q: You see a word with oo in it. You should ___.
options: try one sound, then the other
quizzes.a: try one sound, then the other
quizzes.why: One of the two will be a word you know.

quizzes.q: Which of these is a tricky word?
quizzes.why: The other three follow the sounds.

quizzes.q: Before you decide a word is tricky, you should ___.
quizzes.why: Most English words do follow the sounds.

teacherNotes.note: Every pattern card has a worked example, every practice has a key, and every speaking task ends with record, listen back, check.

This is the whole unit, and it goes against everything Units 2 to 7 taught. Expect a learner to read the letters separately for a while. Do not explain it again; point at the pair and say the one sound, and have them say it back. It is a habit, and habits are built by repetition, not by argument.

teacherNotes.type: Find the pair before reading, not during
teacherNotes.note: Left-to-right letter-by-letter reading breaks on these words, because the learner commits to the first letter's sound before they have seen the second. The move is to scan the word for the pair first. A finger under the pair is enough. It looks like a crutch and it is the skill.

From here to the end of the level there are always more letters than sounds. A learner who counts letters will write a spare letter into every word. Have them say the word and count on their fingers before they write.

teacherNotes.type: The long-short pairs are the fastest way in
teacherNotes.note: Said alone, a long vowel is just a sound. Said beside its short partner it is a contrast, and contrasts are what ears learn. Use fit and feet, got and goat, cat and wait. Two seconds each and it does more than a minute of drilling one.

teacherNotes.type: oo is genuinely ambiguous, so teach the strategy not the answer
teacherNotes.note: There is no reliable rule for boot against foot. The move is to try the long sound, ask whether it made a word, and try the short one if it did not. A learner who has that strategy is never stuck; one who is waiting for the rule is stuck on every oo word.

teacherNotes.type: who, love and have are the first real exceptions
teacherNotes.note: Everything called tricky so far has been common and short. These three break the sounds outright, and it is worth saying that English has perhaps a hundred words like this and they are nearly all words you meet every day. That is reassuring and it is true.

assignment.title: Read and write the new words
assignment.instructions:
Two parts.
1. Record yourself. Say the sound for each new spelling.
Then read these words, slowly and then faster:
wait, feet, pie, boat, boot, foot
2. Write six of the words from their sounds.
Beside each one, write how many sounds it has.
Listen back before you finish.
assignment.submissionType: Audio recording and a written page
